record.original_question: Let $A$ be an $n x n$ random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian (or Rademacher, or Bernoulli) entries, and take any $n$-dimensional vector $b$. Is it possible (conditioned on a high-probability event) to solve the linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy faster than $O(n^omega)$?

evidence.quote: Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian (or Rademacher, or Bernoulli) entries, and take any $n$-dimensional vector $b$. Is it possible (conditioned on a high-probability event) to solve the linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy faster than $O(n^\omega)$?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the exponent of square matrix multiplication, i.e., the infimum of all real numbers $\tau$ such that two $n \times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{R}$ can be multiplied using $O(n^\tau)$ arithmetic operations.

Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ random matrix whose entries are independent and identically distributed, drawn from one of the following distributions:
(i) the standard Gaussian $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$;
(ii) the Rademacher distribution (uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$);
(iii) the Bernoulli distribution (uniform on $\{0,1\}$, or with parameter $1/2$).

Let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be an arbitrary (deterministic) vector. Consider the task of computing, to high accuracy (say to within additive error $2^{-\mathrm{poly}(n)}$ in some natural norm), a vector $x$ satisfying $Ax = b$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, conditioned on an event of probability $1 - o(1)$ over the randomness of $A$, solves the linear system $Ax = b$ to high accuracy in time $O(n^{\omega - \varepsilon})$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$ (in either the arithmetic or bit complexity model)?
artifact.category_tag: Random linear systems and matrix multiplication exponent
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of solving an $n\times n$ dense linear system faster than $O(n^\omega)$ remains open. Peng and Vempala (SODA 2021; JACM 2024) gave an algorithm beating matrix multiplication for sparse linear systems (with $o(n^{(\omega-1)/\log\kappa(A)})$ nonzeros and polynomial condition number), but no analogous result is known for dense random matrices with i.i.d. Gaussian/Rademacher/Bernoulli entries. The dense random case appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Solving Sparse Linear Systems Faster than Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: We present an algorithm that solves linear systems in sparse matrices asymptotically faster than matrix multiplication for any ω > 2.
status_evidence.claim: Progress for sparse matrices, but the general/dense problem of beating n^ω remains open.
